prompt: On a typical Connecticut interstate highway, unless a different limit is posted, the maximum speed limit is:
options: 55 mph
65 mph
70 mph
75 mph
explanation: Connecticut interstates are generally posted at 65 mph, though some urban or work-zone segments are lower. Always obey the posted sign.

prompt: Under Connecticut's zero-tolerance law, a driver under 21 can be charged with operating under the influence with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) as low as:
explanation: Connecticut sets a 0.02% BAC limit for drivers under 21. For drivers 21 and over the limit is 0.08%, and for commercial drivers it is 0.04%.

prompt: In Connecticut, your driver's license may be suspended for accumulating how many points on your driving record?
options: 6 or more points in any rolling 6-month window
4 or more points in 12 months
10 or more points within 24 months
12 or more points at any time
explanation: The Connecticut DMV sends a warning letter at 6 points and may suspend your license once you reach 10 or more points within a 24-month period.

prompt: During the FIRST six months after a 16- or 17-year-old gets a Connecticut license, who may ride as a passenger?
options: No passengers at all under any circumstances
Only the parents or legal guardian, or a licensed driving instructor
Any friends, up to three at a time
Anyone as long as they are over 20
explanation: For the first six months, a newly licensed 16- or 17-year-old may carry only a parent/legal guardian (at least one of whom holds a valid license) or a licensed driving instructor. Immediate family may be added during the second six months.

11 p.m. to 5 a.m.
10 p.m. to 6 a.m.

Hold the phone only at red lights
Use the phone hands-free; holding a handheld phone while driving is prohibited
explanation: Connecticut prohibits the use of handheld mobile devices while driving. Drivers 18 and older may use hands-free technology; drivers under 18 may not use any mobile device, even hands-free.

Speed up to clear the area quickly
Stop completely until the vehicle leaves
Slow down and, when it is safe, move over one lane away from the vehicle
explanation: The Move Over law requires drivers to reduce speed and, when it is safe to do so, change lanes to leave an empty lane next to a stopped emergency, maintenance, or tow vehicle showing flashing lights.

options: The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
The larger vehicle
Whoever accelerates first
explanation: When two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

options: Stop, then proceed when it is safe, as at a stop sign
Speed up to clear the intersection
Slow down and proceed with caution
Stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to green
explanation: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a complete stop, then proceed when the way is clear.

Mark a work zone only
Provide route, distance and destination information for travelers ahead
Warn you of a possible hazard or a change in road conditions ahead
explanation: Yellow diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to conditions ahead such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings so you can slow down and prepare.

Pass on the left if no children are visible
explanation: Drivers approaching from either direction on an undivided road must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, and stay stopped until the bus resumes motion or the lights stop.
